key_insight: AI assistance improved readers’ ECG differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI, with a modest additional benefit from Grad-CAM heatmaps.
clinical_relevance: ECG-based AI could support this diagnostic distinction, but the study does not establish safety or benefit in real-time emergency care.
method: Developed a three-model deep learning ensemble using 12-lead ECG images from two hospitals.
Used self-supervised pretraining, fine-tuning, and external validation.
Studied 70 healthcare providers across four phases, including randomized comparison of reference sheets, AI predictions, and AI plus heatmaps.
evidence_signal: External-validation accuracy was 91.4% for Takotsubo–STEMI discrimination; estimated reader correctness rose from 63.2% unaided to 86.4% with AI assistance.
watch_item: ECGs were recorded up to 14 days after symptom onset regardless of reperfusion status, limiting extrapolation to initial emergency triage.
paper_title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis
